fix_commit.message: avcodec/bsf/extract_extradata: Check that block_size is not negative
fix_commit.author: Michael Niedermayer

findings.title: Integer overflow in LCEVC payload_size computation leads to out-of-bounds access
findings.message: In write_lcevc_nalu(), payload_size is declared as a plain 'int' but can be populated from get_mb(), which returns a uint64_t multi-byte-encoded value that can be arbitrarily large (up to 70 bits of accumulated data). When assigned to the int payload_size, the value truncates/overflows and can become negative or otherwise attacker-controlled in ways that break the subsequent arithmetic. block_size = raw_block_size = payload_size + (get_bits_count(&gb) >> 3) can then overflow to a negative int. The subsequent bounds check 'if (block_size >= bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gbc)) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;' only rejects large positive values; a negative block_size passes this check. block_size is then used in bytestream2_tell(&gbc) + block_size to compute block_end, and used directly in bytestream2_put_buffer(pbc, raw_gbc.buffer, raw_block_size) and bytestream2_skip(&gbc, block_size)/bytestream2_skip(&raw_gbc, raw_block_size), which with a negative/wrapped size causes an out-of-bounds read from the NAL buffer (as observed by the fuzzer), and can drive the state machine into a memory-unsafe path.
findings.suggestion: Store payload_size in a wide unsigned type (e.g. uint64_t) as returned by get_mb(), and before computing block_size, explicitly check that payload_size does not exceed INT_MAX minus the current byte offset (get_bits_count(&gb) >> 3) to prevent signed integer overflow/truncation, returning AVERROR_INVALIDDATA if it would overflow, before doing the addition and the bytestream2_get_bytes_left comparison.

ground_truth.root_cause: The code introduced in the LCEVC extradata support used a 32-bit signed int to hold a payload size read via a multi-byte/variable length decoder (get_mb, uint64_t) without validating that the value fits within range before using it in pointer/length arithmetic, allowing signed integer overflow and a negative computed block_size to bypass the sanity check that only guarded against overly large (not negative) sizes.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Integer overflow in LCEVC payload_size computation leads to out-of-bounds access
